sanskrit: pūrṇe caturdaśe varṣe pañcabhyāṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ bharadvājāśramaṃ prāpya vavande niyato munim
english: At the completion of the fourteenth year plus five nights, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa arrived at the hermitage of Bharadvāja and reverently saluted the sage with self-restraint.

sanskrit: so 'pṛcchad abhivādyainaṃ bharadvājaṃ tapodhanam śṛṇoṣi ka cid bhagavan subhikṣānāmayaṃ pure kaccic ca yukto bharato jīvanty api ca mātaraḥ
english: Having paid homage to Bharadvāja, the treasure of asceticism, he asked him: "O blessed one, do you hear any news of prosperity and health in the city? And is Bharata well? Do my mothers still live?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa bharadvājo mahāmuniḥ pratyuvāca raghuśreṣṭhaṃ smitapūrvaṃ prahṛṣṭavat
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, the great sage Bharadvāja replied to the foremost of the Raghu clan with a smile, appearing joyful.

sanskrit: paṅkadigdhas tu bharato jaṭilas tvāṃ pratīkṣate pāduke te puraskṛtya sarvaṃ ca kuśalaṃ gṛhe
english: "Bharata, smeared with mud and wearing matted locks, awaits you, having placed your sandals before him in honour; all is well in the household."

sanskrit: tvāṃ purā cīravasanaṃ praviśantaṃ mahāvanam strītṛtīyaṃ cyutaṃ rājyād dharmakāmaṃ ca kevalam
english: "You who had entered the great forest wearing bark garments long ago — fallen from the kingdom with a woman as your third companion, devoted solely to righteousness —"

sanskrit: padātiṃ tyaktasarvasvaṃ pitur vacanakāriṇam svargabhogaiḥ parityaktaṃ svargacyutam ivāmaram
english: "— going on foot, having renounced everything, acting upon your father's command, bereft of the enjoyments of heaven, like an immortal fallen from heaven —"

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu karuṇā pūrvaṃ mamāsīt samitiṃjaya kaikeyīvacane yuktaṃ vanyamūlaphalāśanam
english: "— seeing you thus, O conqueror in battle, compassion arose in me before, subsisting on forest roots and fruits because of Kaikeyī's command —"

sanskrit: sāmprataṃ susamṛddhārthaṃ samitragaṇabāndhavam samīkṣya vijitāriṃ tvāṃ mama prītir anuttamā
english: "— but now, seeing you who have achieved your full purpose, surrounded by companions and kinsmen, with your enemies conquered, my joy is unsurpassed."

sanskrit: sarvaṃ ca sukhaduḥkhaṃ te viditaṃ mama rāghava yat tvayā vipulaṃ prāptaṃ janasthānavadhādikam
english: "All your joys and sorrows are known to me, O Rāghava — all that you have abundantly endured, beginning with the slaughter at Janasthāna."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇārthe niyuktasya rakṣataḥ sarvatāpasān mārīcadarśanaṃ caiva sītonmathanam eva ca
english: "Your deployment in the service of the brāhmaṇas, your protection of all the ascetics, the encounter with Mārīca, and the abduction of Sītā —"

sanskrit: kabandhadarśanaṃ caiva pampābhigamanaṃ tathā sugrīveṇa ca te sakhyaṃ yac ca vālī hatas tvayā
english: "— the meeting with Kabandha, your approach to the Pampā lake, your alliance with Sugrīva, and how Vālī was slain by you —"

sanskrit: mārgaṇaṃ caiva vaidehyāḥ karma vātātmajasya ca viditāyāṃ ca vaidehyāṃ nalasetur yathā kṛtaḥ yathā ca dīpitā laṅkā prahṛṣṭair hariyūthapaiḥ
english: "— the search for the daughter of Videha, the deeds of the son of the wind-god, and upon the discovery of the daughter of Videha, how the bridge of Nala was built, and how Laṅkā was set ablaze by the exultant monkey leaders —"

sanskrit: saputrabāndhavāmātyaḥ sabalaḥ saha vāhanaḥ yathā ca nihataḥ saṃkhye rāvaṇo devakaṇṭakaḥ
english: "— and how Rāvaṇa, the tormentor of the gods, was slain in battle along with his sons, kinsmen, ministers, forces, and vehicles —"

sanskrit: samāgamaś ca tridaśair yathādattaś ca te varaḥ sarvaṃ mamaitad viditaṃ tapasā dharmavatsala
english: "— and the meeting with the thirty gods, and the boons granted to you — all of this is known to me by my ascetic power, O beloved of righteousness."

sanskrit: aham apy atra te dadmi varaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ vara arghyaṃ pratigṛhāṇedam ayodhyāṃ śvo gamiṣyasi
english: "I too grant you a boon here, O best among those who bear weapons — accept this guest-offering; tomorrow you shall go to Ayodhyā."

sanskrit: tasya tac chirasā vākyaṃ pratigṛhya nṛpātmajaḥ bāḍham ity eva saṃhṛṣṭaḥ śrīmān varam ayācata
english: Accepting those words with a bowed head, the glorious son of the king, greatly rejoiced, said "So be it" and then requested a boon.

sanskrit: akālaphalino vṛkṣāḥ sarve cāpi madhusravāḥ bhavantu mārge bhagavann ayodhyāṃ prati gacchataḥ
english: "May all the trees along the road as I travel toward Ayodhyā, O blessed one, bear fruit out of season and drip with honey."

sanskrit: niṣphalāḥ phalinaś cāsan vipuṣpāḥ puṣpaśālinaḥ śuṣkāḥ samagrapatrās te nagāś caiva madhusravāḥ
english: Those trees that were fruitless bore fruit; those without flowers bloomed; the dry trees became fully leafed; and all those trees dripped with honey.

sanskrit: ayodhyāṃ tu samālokya cintayām āsa rāghavaḥ cintayitvā tato dṛṣṭiṃ vānareṣu nyapātayat
english: Gazing toward Ayodhyā, Rāghava fell into reflection; having reflected, he then turned his gaze upon the monkeys.

sanskrit: priyakāmaḥ priyaṃ rāmas tatas tvaritavikramam uvāca dhīmāṃs tejasvī hanūmantaṃ plavaṃgamam
english: Rāma, the wise and resplendent one, wishing to do what was dear, then spoke to Hanūmān the monkey, swift in his stride, for a cherished purpose.

sanskrit: ayodhyāṃ tvarito gaccha kṣipraṃ tvaṃ plavagottama jānīhi kaccit kuśalī jano nṛpatimandire
english: "Go swiftly to Ayodhyā, O best of leaping ones; quickly find out whether the people in the king's palace are well."

sanskrit: śṛṅgaverapuraṃ prāpya guhaṃ gahanagocaram niṣādādhipatiṃ brūhi kuśalaṃ vacanān mama
english: "Reaching Śṛṅgaverapura, tell Guha who moves in the forest thickets — the lord of the Niṣādas — of my well-being, conveying my words."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu māṃ kuśalinam arogaṃ vigatajvaram bhaviṣyati guhaḥ prītaḥ sa mamātmasamaḥ sakhā
english: "Upon hearing that I am well, free from illness and free from anxiety, Guha will be pleased — he is a friend dear to me as my own self."

sanskrit: ayodhyāyāś ca te mārgaṃ pravṛttiṃ bharatasya ca nivedayiṣyati prīto niṣādādhipatir guhaḥ
english: "The pleased lord of the Niṣādas, Guha, will show you the road to Ayodhyā and inform you of the news concerning Bharata."

sanskrit: bharatas tu tvayā vācyaḥ kuśalaṃ vacanān mama siddhārthaṃ śaṃsa māṃ tasmai sabhāryaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam
english: "You must tell Bharata of my well-being in my own words; announce to him that I have accomplished my purpose, along with my wife and together with Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: haraṇaṃ cāpi vaidehyā rāvaṇena balīyasā sugrīveṇa ca saṃvādaṃ vālinaś ca vadhaṃ raṇe
english: "Tell him also of the abduction of the daughter of Videha by the mighty Rāvaṇa, of my alliance with Sugrīva, and of the slaying of Vālī in battle."

sanskrit: maithilyanveṣaṇaṃ caiva yathā cādhigatā tvayā laṅghayitvā mahātoyam āpagāpatim avyayam
english: "Tell him of the search for the daughter of Mithilā, and how she was found by you after leaping over the great waters of the eternal ocean-lord."

sanskrit: upayānaṃ samudrasya sāgarasya ca darśanam yathā ca kāritaḥ setū rāvaṇaś ca yathā hataḥ
english: "Tell of the approach to the ocean and the sighting of the sea, how the bridge was caused to be built, and how Rāvaṇa was slain."

sanskrit: varadānaṃ mahendreṇa brahmaṇā varuṇena ca mahādevaprasādāc ca pitrā mama samāgamam
english: "Tell of the granting of boons by great Indra, by Brahmā, by Varuṇa, and of my meeting with my father through the grace of Mahādeva."

sanskrit: jitvā śatrugaṇān rāmaḥ prāpya cānuttamaṃ yaśaḥ upayāti samṛddhārthaḥ saha mitrair mahābalaḥ
english: "Rāma, having conquered the hosts of enemies and having attained unsurpassed glory, comes having fully accomplished his purpose, with his mighty allies."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā yamākāraṃ bhajate bharatas tataḥ sa ca te veditavyaḥ syāt sarvaṃ yac cāpi māṃ prati
english: "Observe what expression Bharata assumes upon hearing this; and you must also ascertain everything regarding him and whatever pertains to me."

sanskrit: jñeyāḥ sarve ca vṛttāntā bharatasyeṅgitāni ca tattvena mukhavarṇena dṛṣṭyā vyābhāṣaṇena ca
english: "All of Bharata's circumstances and gestures must be discerned truly — by his facial colour, his glance, and his manner of speaking."

sanskrit: sarvakāmasamṛddhaṃ hi hastyaśvarathasaṃkulam pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyaṃ kasya nāvartayen manaḥ
english: "For whose mind would not be turned by a kingdom filled with every desire, teeming with elephants, horses, and chariots — the realm inherited from father and grandfather?"

sanskrit: saṃgatyā bharataḥ śrīmān rājyenārthī svayaṃ bhavet praśāstu vasudhāṃ sarvām akhilāṃ raghunandanaḥ
english: "It may be that the glorious Bharata, by circumstance, has himself come to desire the kingdom; let the son of the Raghu line rule the entire earth without exception."

sanskrit: tasya buddhiṃ ca vijñāya vyavasāyaṃ ca vānara yāvan na dūraṃ yātāḥ smaḥ kṣipram āgantum arhasi
english: "Having ascertained his intention and resolve, O monkey, you should return quickly, before we have travelled far."

sanskrit: iti pratisamādiṣṭo hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ mānuṣaṃ dhārayan rūpam ayodhyāṃ tvarito yayau
english: Having thus been instructed, Hanūmān the son of the wind-god, assuming a human form, went swiftly to Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: laṅghayitvā pitṛpathaṃ bhujagendrālayaṃ śubham gaṅgāyamunayor bhīmaṃ saṃnipātam atītya ca
english: He leapt over the path of the ancestors, the beautiful abode of the lord of serpents, and crossed the fearsome confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā.

sanskrit: śṛṅgaverapuraṃ prāpya guham āsādya vīryavān sa vācā śubhayā hṛṣṭo hanūmān idam abravīt
english: Reaching Śṛṅgaverapura and finding Guha, the mighty Hanūmān, filled with joy, spoke these words with auspicious speech:

sanskrit: sakhā tu tava kākutstho rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ sasītaḥ saha saumitriḥ sa tvāṃ kuśalam abravīt
english: "Your friend Kākutstha Rāma, whose valour is truth, together with Sītā and with the son of Sumitrā, sends you his greetings of well-being."

sanskrit: pañcamīm adya rajanīm uṣitvā vacanān muneḥ bharadvājābhyanujñātaṃ drakṣyasy adyaiva rāghavam
english: "Having spent tonight, the fifth night, on the word of the sage, with the leave of Bharadvāja, you shall see Rāghava this very day."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejāḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ utpapāta mahāvego vegavān avicārayan
english: Having spoken thus, the greatly resplendent one, with his bodily hairs thrilling with delight, the swift one leapt up swiftly and without hesitation.

sanskrit: so 'paśyad rāmatīrthaṃ ca nadīṃ vālukinīṃ tathā gomatīṃ tāṃ ca so 'paśyad bhīmaṃ sālavanaṃ tathā
english: He saw the ford of Rāma, and also the sandy river Vālukinī; he saw too the Gomatī, and the fearsome forest of sāla trees.

sanskrit: sa gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ tvaritaḥ kapikuñjaraḥ āsasāda drumān phullān nandigrāmasamīpajān
english: Having travelled a great distance in haste, that elephant among monkeys came upon the blossoming trees growing near Nandigrāma.

sanskrit: krośamātre tv ayodhyāyāś cīrakṛṣṇājināmbaram dadarśa bharataṃ dīnaṃ kṛśam āśramavāsinam
english: At a distance of barely one krośa from Ayodhyā, he saw Bharata, emaciated and sorrowful, dwelling like a forest hermit, wearing bark cloth and black antelope skin.

sanskrit: jaṭilaṃ maladigdhāṅgaṃ bhrātṛvyasanakarśitam phalamūlāśinaṃ dāntaṃ tāpasaṃ dharmacāriṇam
english: He was wearing matted locks, his body smeared with grime, emaciated by grief over his brother, subsisting on fruits and roots, self-controlled, an ascetic, walking the path of righteousness.

sanskrit: samunnatajaṭābhāraṃ valkalājinavāsasaṃ niyataṃ bhāvitātmānaṃ brahmarṣisamatejasaṃ
english: He bore a high mass of matted locks, wore garments of bark and antelope skin, was disciplined in conduct, had a cultivated inner self, and possessed a brilliance equal to that of a brahmarṣi.

sanskrit: pāduke te puraskṛtya śāsantaṃ vai vasuṃdharām caturvarṇyasya lokasya trātāraṃ sarvato bhayāt
english: Having placed your sandals before him as regent, he was governing the earth and protecting the world of all four classes from every fear.

sanskrit: upasthitam amātyaiś ca śucibhiś ca purohitaiḥ balamukhyaiś ca yuktaiś ca kāṣāyāmbaradhāribhiḥ
english: He was attended by pure ministers, by the court priest, and by the chiefs of the army, all of them disciplined and wearing ochre robes.

sanskrit: na hi te rājaputraṃ taṃ cīrakṛṣṇājināmbaram parimoktuṃ vyavasyanti paurā vai dharmavatsalāḥ
english: The citizens, devoted to righteousness, were indeed not willing to let that prince go — he who wore bark cloth and black antelope skin.

sanskrit: taṃ dharmam iva dharmajñaṃ devavantam ivāparam uvāca prāñjalir vākyaṃ hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: To him who was like righteousness incarnate, knowing righteousness, like another one accompanied by the gods, Hanūmān the son of the wind-god spoke with joined palms:

sanskrit: vasantaṃ daṇḍakāraṇye yaṃ tvaṃ cīrajaṭādharam anuśocasi kākutsthaṃ sa tvā kuśalam abravīt
english: "The Kākutstha whom you mourn — the one who dwelt in the Daṇḍaka forest wearing bark garments and matted locks — that one sends his greetings of well-being to you."

sanskrit: priyam ākhyāmi te deva śokaṃ tyakṣyasi dāruṇam asmin muhūrte bhrātrā tvaṃ rāmeṇa saha saṃgataḥ
english: "I announce joyful news to you, O lord — you will cast off your terrible grief; at this very moment you shall be united with your brother Rāma."

sanskrit: nihatya rāvaṇaṃ rāmaḥ pratilabhya ca maithilīm upayāti samṛddhārthaḥ saha mitrair mahābalaiḥ
english: "Rāma, having slain Rāvaṇa and having recovered the daughter of Mithilā, comes having fully accomplished his purpose, together with his mighty allies."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaś ca mahātejā vaidehī ca yaśasvinī sītā samagrā rāmeṇa mahendreṇa śacī yathā
english: "The greatly resplendent Lakṣmaṇa and the illustrious Vaidehī Sītā come together with Rāma — as Śacī comes with the great Indra."

sanskrit: evam ukto hanumatā bharataḥ kaikayīsutaḥ papāta sahasā hṛṣṭo harṣān mohaṃ jagāma ha
english: Thus addressed by Hanūmān, Bharata the son of Kaikeyī suddenly fell down in joy; overcome by rapture he fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād utthāya pratyāśvasya ca rāghavaḥ hanūmantam uvācedaṃ bharataḥ priyavādinam
english: Then, after a moment, Bharata the Rāghava rose up and, having recovered, spoke these words to Hanūmān who had spoken such cherished news:

sanskrit: aśokajaiḥ prītimayaiḥ kapim āliṅgya saṃbhramāt siṣeca bharataḥ śrīmān vipulair aśrubindubhiḥ
english: The glorious Bharata, in his excitement, embraced the monkey and, overjoyed as though freed from sorrow, drenched him with copious drops of tears.

sanskrit: devo vā mānuṣo vā tvam anukrośād ihāgataḥ priyākhyānasya te saumya dadāmi bruvataḥ priyam
english: "Whether you are a god or a human who has come here out of compassion, O gentle one, I give you whatever you desire as a reward for announcing this cherished news."

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasraṃ ca grāmāṇāṃ ca śataṃ param sakuṇḍalāḥ śubhācārā bhāryāḥ kanyāś ca ṣoḍaśa
english: "A hundred thousand cows, a hundred excellent villages, sixteen wives who are nobly born and well-mannered, adorned with earrings —"

sanskrit: hemavarṇāḥ sunāsorūḥ śaśisaumyānanāḥ striyaḥ sarvābharaṇasaṃpannā saṃpannāḥ kulajātibhiḥ
english: "— women of golden complexion, with beautiful noses and thighs, with faces as gentle as the moon, adorned with all ornaments, and endowed with noble birth."

sanskrit: niśamya rāmāgamanaṃ nṛpātmajaḥ kapipravīrasya tadādbhutopamam praharṣito rāmadidṛkṣayābhavat punaś ca harṣād idam abravīd vacaḥ
english: Having heard the wonderful account of Rāma's coming from that best of monkeys, the son of the king was filled with delight and with eagerness to see Rāma; and again, from sheer joy, he spoke these words:

sanskrit: bahūni nāma varṣāṇi gatasya sumahad vanam śṛṇomy ahaṃ prītikaraṃ mama nāthasya kīrtanam
english: "For many years now, since my lord went to the great forest, I hear the glad recounting of my lord's deeds with joy."

sanskrit: kalyāṇī bata gātheyaṃ laukikī pratibhāti me eti jīvantam ānando naraṃ varṣaśatād api
english: "Auspicious indeed does this popular saying appear to me: joy comes to a man still living, even after a hundred years."

sanskrit: rāghavasya harīṇāṃ ca katham āsīt samāgamaḥ kasmin deśe kim āśritya tat tvam ākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ
english: "How did the meeting of Rāghava and the monkeys come about? In what region, through reliance on what? Tell me who am asking you this."

sanskrit: sa pṛṣṭo rājaputreṇa bṛsyāṃ samupaveśitaḥ ācacakṣe tataḥ sarvaṃ rāmasya caritaṃ vane
english: Being asked by the prince and seated on a cushioned seat, Hanūmān then recounted the full story of Rāma's deeds in the forest.

sanskrit: yathā pravrajito rāmo mātur datte vare tava yathā ca putraśokena rājā daśaratho mṛtaḥ
english: How Rāma was exiled when the boon was granted to your mother; and how King Daśaratha died of grief for his son —

sanskrit: yathā dūtais tvam ānītas tūrṇaṃ rājagṛhāt prabho tvayāyodhyāṃ praviṣṭena yathā rājyaṃ na cepsitam
english: How you were quickly summoned by messengers from the royal household, O lord; and how, upon your return to Ayodhyā, you refused to accept the kingdom —

sanskrit: citrakūṭaṃ giriṃ gatvā rājyenāmitrakarśanaḥ nimantritas tvayā bhrātā dharmam ācaritā satām
english: How you went to Mount Citrakūṭa and invited your brother who was afflicting enemies with the kingdom; how he practised the conduct of the good —

sanskrit: sthitena rājño vacane yathā rājyaṃ visarjitam āryasya pāduke gṛhya yathāsi punar āgataḥ
english: How, steadfast in the king's command, he renounced the kingdom; and how you returned, having taken the sandals of your elder brother —

sanskrit: sarvam etan mahābāho yathāvad viditaṃ tava tvayi pratiprayāte tu yad vṛttaṃ tan nibodha me
english: "All of this, O great-armed one, is known to you as it happened; but now hear from me what occurred after your departure."

sanskrit: apayāte tvayi tadā samudbhrāntamṛgadvijam praviveśātha vijanaṃ sumahad daṇḍakāvanam
english: After your departure at that time, they entered the great and deserted Daṇḍaka forest, where the deer and birds were startled and scattered.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ purastād balavān gacchatāṃ gahane vane vinadan sumahānādaṃ virādhaḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Before them as they went through the dense forest, Virādha appeared, powerful and roaring with a great roar.

sanskrit: tam utkṣipya mahānādam ūrdhvabāhum adhomukham nikhāte prakṣipanti sma nadantam iva kuñjaram
english: Lifting him up while he roared loudly, with his arms raised and his face downward, they hurled him into a pit dug in the ground — like an elephant bellowing.

sanskrit: tat kṛtvā duṣkaraṃ karma bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau sāyāhne śarabhaṅgasya ramyam āśramam īyatuḥ
english: Having accomplished that difficult deed, the two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, at evening, went to the beautiful hermitage of Śarabhaṅga.

sanskrit: śarabhaṅge divaṃ prāpte rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ abhivādya munīn sarvāñ janasthānam upāgamat
english: When Śarabhaṅga had gone to heaven, Rāma of true valour, having reverenced all the sages, went on to Janasthāna.

sanskrit: caturdaśasahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām hatāni vasatā tatra rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
english: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of fearsome deeds were slain while the great-souled Rāghava dwelt there.

sanskrit: tataḥ paścāc chūrpaṇakhā rāmapārśvam upāgatā tato rāmeṇa saṃdiṣṭo lakṣmaṇaḥ sahasotthitaḥ
english: After that, Śūrpaṇakhā came to Rāma's side; then, directed by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa swiftly rose up —

sanskrit: pragṛhya khaḍgaṃ ciccheda karṇanāse mahābalaḥ tatas tenārditā bālā rāvaṇaṃ samupāgatā
english: — and that mighty one, drawing his sword, cut off her ears and nose. Tormented by him, that wretched woman then went to Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: rāvaṇānucaro ghoro mārīco nāma rākṣasaḥ lobhayām āsa vaidehīṃ bhūtvā ratnamayo mṛgaḥ
english: Mārīca, a terrible rākṣasa and follower of Rāvaṇa, enticed the daughter of Videha by becoming a gem-studded deer.

sanskrit: sā rāmam abravīd dṛṣṭvā vaidehī gṛhyatām iti aho manoharaḥ kānta āśrame no bhaviṣyati
english: She, the daughter of Videha, upon seeing it, said to Rāma: "Capture it — ah, what a beautiful creature it would be in our hermitage, my beloved!"

sanskrit: tato rāmo dhanuṣpāṇir dhāvantam anudhāvati sa taṃ jaghāna dhāvantaṃ śareṇānataparvaṇā
english: Then Rāma, bow in hand, ran after it as it ran; he struck it as it ran with an arrow with straight joints.

sanskrit: atha saumyā daśagrīvo mṛgaṃ yāte tu rāghave lakṣmaṇe cāpi niṣkrānte praviveśāśramaṃ tadā jagrāha tarasā sītāṃ grahaḥ khe rohiṇīm iva
english: Then, O gentle one, when Rāghava had gone after the deer and Lakṣmaṇa too had gone out, the ten-necked one entered the hermitage and seized Sītā by force — as the planet Rāhu seizes Rohiṇī in the sky.

sanskrit: trātukāmaṃ tato yuddhe hatvā gṛdhraṃ jaṭāyuṣam pragṛhya sītāṃ sahasā jagāmāśu sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Then, after slaying in battle the vulture Jaṭāyu who sought to protect her, Rāvaṇa seized Sītā and swiftly departed at once.

sanskrit: tatas tv adbhutasaṃkāśāḥ sthitāḥ parvatamūrdhani sītāṃ gṛhītvā gacchantaṃ vānarāḥ parvatopamāḥ dadṛśur vismitās tatra rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam
english: Then monkeys of wondrous appearance, standing on the mountain peak, resembling mountains themselves, saw there with amazement Rāvaṇa the lord of rākṣasas, carrying Sītā and departing.

sanskrit: praviverśa tadā laṅkāṃ rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ
english: Then Rāvaṇa who makes the world cry out entered Laṅkā.

sanskrit: tāṃ suvarṇaparikrānte śubhe mahati veśmani praveśya maithilīṃ vākyaiḥ sāntvayām āsa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Having brought the daughter of Mithilā into that auspicious and great mansion surrounded by gold, Rāvaṇa tried to console her with words.

sanskrit: nivartamānaḥ kākutstho dṛṣṭvā gṛdhraṃ pravivyathe
english: Kākutstha, returning, was filled with anguish when he saw the vulture.

sanskrit: gṛdhraṃ hataṃ tadā dagdhvā rāmaḥ priyasakhaṃ pituḥ godāvarīm anucaran vanoddeśāṃś ca puṣpitān āsedatur mahāraṇye kabandhaṃ nāma rākṣasaṃ
english: Having cremated the slain vulture, his father's dear friend, Rāma, wandering along the Godāvarī and through the flowering forest regions, together with his companion came upon a rākṣasa in the great forest named Kabandha.

sanskrit: tataḥ kabandhavacanād rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ ṛśyamūkaṃ giriṃ gatvā sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ
english: Then, on Kabandha's counsel, Rāma of true valour went to Mount Ṛśyamūka and met Sugrīva.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samāgamaḥ pūrvaṃ prītyā hārdo vyajāyata itaretara saṃvādāt pragāḍhaḥ praṇayas tayoḥ
english: Their meeting at first was cordial from the heart; through mutual conversation a deep affection grew between those two.

sanskrit: rāmaḥ svabāhuvīryeṇa svarājyaṃ pratyapādayat vālinaṃ samare hatvā mahākāyaṃ mahābalam
english: Rāma, by the strength of his own arms, restored his kingdom to him, having slain in battle the great-bodied and mighty Vālī.

sanskrit: sugrīvaḥ sthāpito rājye sahitaḥ sarvavānaraiḥ rāmāya pratijānīte rājaputryās tu mārgaṇam
english: Sugrīva, installed in the kingdom together with all the monkeys, pledged to Rāma the search for the princess.

sanskrit: ādiṣṭā vānarendreṇa sugrīveṇa mahātmanā daśakoṭyaḥ plavaṃgānāṃ sarvāḥ prasthāpitā diśaḥ
english: Commanded by Sugrīva, the great-souled lord of the monkeys, ten crores of monkeys were dispatched in all directions.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ no vipranaṣṭānāṃ vindhye parvatasattame bhṛśaṃ śokābhitaptānāṃ mahān kālo 'tyavartata
english: As for us who had gone astray and lost our way, on the Vindhya, best of mountains, deeply afflicted by grief, a great span of time passed by.

sanskrit: bhrātā tu gṛdhrarājasya saṃpātir nāma vīryavān samākhyāti sma vasatiṃ sītāyā rāvaṇālaye
english: But Saṃpāti the valiant, the brother of the king of vultures, reported to us the dwelling-place of Sītā in Rāvaṇa's abode.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ duḥkhaparītānāṃ duḥkhaṃ tajjñātināṃ nudan ātmavīryaṃ samāsthāya yojanānāṃ śataṃ plutaḥ
english: I, removing the sorrow of those kinsmen who were overwhelmed with sorrow, mustering my own strength, leapt a hundred yojanas.

sanskrit: tatrāham ekām adrākṣam aśokavanikāṃ gatām kauśeyavastrāṃ malināṃ nirānandāṃ dṛḍhavratām
english: There I saw her alone, having entered the Aśoka grove, wearing silken garments that were soiled, joyless but firm in her resolve.

sanskrit: tayā sametya vidhivat pṛṣṭvā sarvam aninditām abhijñānaṃ maṇiṃ labdhvā caritārtho 'ham āgataḥ
english: Having met with her according to proper form, having inquired of that blameless one about everything, having received the jewel as a token of recognition, I returned with my purpose accomplished.

sanskrit: mayā ca punar āgamya rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ abhijñānaṃ mayā dattam arciṣmān sa mahāmaṇiḥ
english: And upon my return, I gave that resplendent great jewel as the token of recognition to Rāma of unwearied action.

sanskrit: śrutvā tāṃ maithilīṃ hṛṣṭas tv āśaśaṃse sa jīvitam jīvitāntam anuprāptaḥ pītvāmṛtam ivāturaḥ
english: Hearing of that daughter of Mithilā, he rejoiced and affirmed his will to live — he who had reached the end of life's purpose, like a sick man who has drunk nectar.

sanskrit: udyojayiṣyann udyogaṃ dadhre laṅkāvadhe manaḥ jighāṃsur iva lokāṃs te sarvāṃl lokān vibhāvasuḥ
english: Rousing his army to exertion, he set his mind on the destruction of Laṅkā — like fire wishing to consume all those worlds.

sanskrit: tataḥ samudram āsādya nalaṃ setum akārayat atarat kapivīrāṇāṃ vāhinī tena setunā
english: Then reaching the ocean, he caused Nala to build a bridge; the army of heroic monkeys crossed over by that bridge.

sanskrit: prahastam avadhīn nīlaḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ tu rāghavaḥ lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇasutaṃ svayaṃ rāmas tu rāvaṇam
english: Nīla slew Prahasta; Rāghava slew Kumbhakarṇa; Lakṣmaṇa slew the son of Rāvaṇa; and Rāma himself slew Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: sa śakreṇa samāgamya yamena varuṇena ca surarṣibhiś ca kākutstho varāṃl lebhe paraṃtapaḥ
english: Having met with Śakra, with Yama, with Varuṇa, and with the divine sages, Kākutstha the scorcher of enemies received boons.

sanskrit: sa tu dattavaraḥ prītyā vānaraiś ca samāgataḥ puṣpakeṇa vimānena kiṣkindhām abhyupāgamat
english: He, the recipient of those boons, with gladness and accompanied by the monkeys, came to Kiṣkindhā by the aerial chariot Puṣpaka.

sanskrit: taṃ gaṅgāṃ punar āsādya vasantaṃ munisaṃnidhau avighnaṃ puṣyayogena śvo rāmaṃ draṣṭum arhasi
english: Him — who is now again on the Gaṅgā, dwelling in the proximity of the sage, under the auspicious Puṣya conjunction without impediment — you shall see tomorrow.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa satyaṃ hanumadvaco mahan niśamya hṛṣṭo bharataḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ uvāca vāṇīṃ manasaḥ praharṣiṇī cirasya pūrṇaḥ khalu me manorathaḥ
english: Then he, Bharata, having heard the great and true words of Hanūmān, rejoiced with joined palms and spoke words that delighted his heart: "My heart's desire, long cherished, is now at last fulfilled."
